title: Hypertensive Retinopathy: The Ocular Mirror of Systemic Health
summary: Hypertensive retinopathy (HR) represents the spectrum of retinal microvascular changes resulting from systemic hypertension. It serves as a vital clinical indicator of target organ damage and long-term cardiovascular risk.

sections.title: Definition & Overview
sections.content: Hypertensive retinopathy is the primary ocular manifestation of systemic arterial hypertension. It involves a series of pathophysiological changes in the retinal microvasculature, categorized into vasoconstrictive, sclerotic, and exudative phases. Its presence, particularly Grade 3 or 4, is a strong predictor of systemic morbidity, including stroke, myocardial infarction, and renal failure.

sections.title: Pathophysiological Progression
content: Step 1: Vasoconstrictive Phase — Acute BP rise triggers myogenic autoregulation, leading to generalized arteriolar narrowing (vasospasm).
Step 2: Sclerotic Phase — Chronic elevation causes intimal thickening, hyaline degeneration, and muscular hyperplasia, resulting in 'Copper' or 'Silver' wiring.
Step 3: Exudative Phase — Breakdown of the blood-retinal barrier (BRB) leads to leakage of plasma and blood (Hemorrhages, Exudates).
Step 4: Complication Phase — Ischemia and secondary vascular occlusions (RVO, RAM) or optic nerve swelling in malignant HTN.

rows: Focal narrowing and AV nicking (Gunn's sign)
Grade III findings PLUS Optic Disc Edema (Papilledema)
Generalized/focal narrowing, AV nicking, wall opacity

branches: Gunn Sign: Compression of vein at crossing
Salus Sign: Deflection of vein (90 degrees)
Bonnet Sign: Distal banking of the vein

sections.title: Ocular Examination Findings
content: Arteriolar Narrowing: Ratio of arteriole to vein (A/V ratio) reduced from normal 2:3 to 1:2 or less.
Flame Hemorrhages: Located in the Nerve Fiber Layer (NFL).
Cotton Wool Spots (CWS): Focal retinal ischemia in the NFL.
Hard Exudates: Lipid deposits in Henle's layer (Macular Star pattern).
Elschnig Spots: Small black spots surrounded by yellow halos (Choroidal infarcts).
Siegrist Streaks: Linear hyperpigmented streaks along choroidal vessels.

rows: Unilateral; 'Blood and Thunder' fundus; dilated veins
History of radiotherapy; very slow progression

sections.title: EMERGENCY: Grade IV Signs
content: Bilateral Optic Disc Edema (Malignant Hypertension)
Severe Headache and Confusion (Encephalopathy)
Systolic BP >180 mmHg or Diastolic BP >120 mmHg
Chest pain or Shortness of breath (Cardiac Involvement)
Decreased Urine Output (Renal Failure)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup & Investigations
content: 1. Comprehensive BP Profile: Multiple readings/24hr monitoring.
2. Dilated Fundus Exam: Gold standard for grading.
3. OCT Macula/RNFL: To quantify edema or subretinal fluid.
4. Systemic Labs: Serum Creatinine, eGFR, Urinalysis (Proteinuria).
5. EKG/Echocardiogram: Assess for LVH or ischemia.

sections.title: Management & Treatment
content: Chronic HTN: Gradual BP reduction via ACE inhibitors, ARBs, or Calcium Channel Blockers.
Hypertensive Crisis: Immediate hospitalization; reduce MAP by max 25% in first hour to prevent ischemic stroke.
Ocular Complications: Intravitreal Anti-VEGF or Steroids for secondary macular edema.
Laser Photocoagulation: For macroaneurysms if leaking/threatening fovea.

content.explanation: V: Vasoconstriction, E: Exudates (Hard), S: Silver wiring, S: Star (Macular), E: Edema (Disc), L: Light reflex changes.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Exam Tips
content: Hypertensive Choroidopathy (Elschnig spots/Siegrist streaks) is usually seen in acute, severe HTN episodes (e.g., Preeclampsia).
If HR is UNILATERAL, suspect Carotid Artery Stenosis on the side with 'spared' retina (the stenosis protects the eye from high pressure).
Cotton wool spots (CWS) are NOT specific to HTN; they occur in DM, HIV, Anemia, and SLE.
The 'Silver Wire' appearance occurs when the vessel wall becomes so thick and opaque that the blood column is no longer visible.

sections.title: Landmark Studies
content: Beaver Dam Eye Study: Showed prevalence of HR is approx 10% in the general population.
Blue Mountains Eye Study: Linked mild HR signs to increased risk of long-term stroke mortality.
ARIC Study: Demonstrated that retinal vascular caliber changes can predict the development of clinical hypertension.
